has been at the forefront of oncology research and cancer care innovation since 1978. Following the opening of its flagship standalone facility, Moores Cancer Center, on the UC San Diego Health La Jolla campus in 2005, UC San Diego Health has expanded its oncology services to five comprehensive outpatient locations across the region.
National Cancer Institute (NCI)-Designated Comprehensive Cancer Center

, a distinction awarded to cancer centers that demonstrate exceptional achievement in cancer research, clinical care, education, and community impact. Committed to advancing groundbreaking research and delivering exceptional patient-centered care, Moores Cancer Center remains a national leader in oncology innovation. UC San Diego Health and its cancer programs are consistently recognized among the nation's leading health care and oncology organizations, earning accolades from U.S. News & World Report, Vizient, and other respected institutions.

UC San Diego Health is also a Magnet-recognized health system, reflecting its commitment to nursing excellence, professional nursing practice, quality outcomes, innovation, and a culture that supports and empowers the nursing workforce. The
Senior Director of Nursing, Oncology
plays a critical leadership role in advancing these standards of excellence across oncology services.
Senior Director of Nursing, Oncology

oversees all nursing operations within UC San Diego Health's outpatient oncology services, including oncology clinics, infusion services, and radiation oncology. This highly visible leadership role serves as a key member of the Oncology Services and Moores Cancer Center leadership team, providing strategic and operational oversight in support of exceptional patient care, nursing excellence, and organizational goals.
Reporting directly to the
Chief Administrative Officer of Oncology and Radiation Therapy Services
Senior Director of Nursing, Oncology

is a highly experienced executive nursing leader providing responsible for the strategic, clinical, administrative, and operational leadership of nursing services across UC San Diego Health’s comprehensive oncology enterprise.

The Senior Director provides executive oversight for nursing practice and operations across oncology ambulatory clinics, infusion services, and radiation medicine. The position leads through subordinate directors, managers, and other nursing leaders and is accountable for ensuring consistent standards of clinical excellence, patient safety, operational performance, workforce effectiveness, financial stewardship, regulatory compliance, and professional nursing practice across a large, complex, and geographically distributed oncology network.

The Senior Director maintains a matrixed reporting relationship to the Chief Clinical Officer/Chief Nursing Officer for UC San Diego Health and serves as an active member of the Nursing Executive Committee, representing Oncology in enterprise-wide nursing strategy, policy, quality, and professional practice initiatives.

This position requires an accomplished, collaborative, and highly visible executive nursing leader who can successfully navigate a complex academic health system, lead through organizational complexity, and cultivate trusted partnerships across clinical, operational, administrative, and academic constituencies. The successful candidate will demonstrate a strong understanding of oncology care delivery, nursing and clinical operations, physician and interdisciplinary partnerships, organizational culture, workforce strategy, and human resources and labor relations, including effective partnership within a unionized environment. The role also requires an appreciation for the unique clinical, operational, academic, and regulatory complexities of a Comprehensive Cancer Center.

Candidates with demonstrated leadership experience within UC San Diego Health, UC San Diego Oncology, or a similarly complex academic health systems are strongly preferred. Internal candidates who bring established institutional knowledge, demonstrated organizational effectiveness, strong cross-functional relationships, and a proven record of successful leadership within UC San Diego Health are particularly encouraged to apply. Experience navigating UC San Diego Health’s organizational structure, culture, policies, labor environment, and shared governance model will be highly valued.

Highly qualified external candidates are also welcomed and encouraged to apply, particularly those who bring comparable senior or executive nursing leadership experience within complex academic health systems, NCI-designated Comprehensive Cancer Centers, or other nationally recognized oncology programs. External candidates should demonstrate a record of successfully leading large, complex clinical operations; building effective physician, nursing, and administrative partnerships; advancing workforce and organizational priorities; and achieving measurable improvements in quality, safety, patient experience, operational performance, and employee engagement.
Patient Care, Quality, and Nursing Excellence

The Senior Director is accountable for advancing exceptional patient outcomes and ensuring the consistent delivery of safe, high-quality, evidence-based, and patient-centered nursing care throughout Oncology.

The incumbent establishes and sustains high standards of nursing practice and ensures that clinical care, nursing competencies, staffing models, and operational practices support the needs of complex oncology patient populations. The Senior Director promotes an environment in which nurses and interdisciplinary team members have a meaningful voice in clinical practice, shared governance, quality improvement, and innovation.

The Senior Director is accountable for nursing quality, safety, patient experience, operational effectiveness, and responsible stewardship of resources. The incumbent collaborates closely with physicians, APPs, nursing leaders, clinical staff, administrators, and other health care professionals to ensure coordinated, integrated care across the oncology continuum.
The Senior Director serves as an executive resource and trusted advisor to nursing leaders, staff, physicians, APPs, students, and other clinical and administrative partners.
Executive and Administrative Leadership

The Senior Director is expected to be a strategic, data-driven executive; accomplished program developer; experienced operator; and effective change leader. The leader translates organizational strategy into measurable operational priorities and leads complex initiatives across multiple clinical environments and organizational structures.

The position has significant responsibility for nursing department budgets, workforce planning, resource allocation, productivity, capital and operational planning, and overall financial performance. The Senior Director ensures resources are deployed effectively and responsibly while maintaining the highest standards of patient care, quality, safety, workforce engagement, and operational performance.

The incumbent recognizes that excellence requires continuous learning, innovation, accountability, and improvement and establishes an environment in which leaders and teams are empowered to identify opportunities, implement sustainable change, and achieve measurable results.

The Senior Director participates with executive leadership in developing and executing short- and long-term organizational strategies and ensures subordinate leaders possess the change-management capabilities necessary to support an agile, resilient, and high-performing workforce.
Culture, Collaboration, and Emotional Intelligence

Exceptional interpersonal effectiveness and a high degree of emotional intelligence are essential to success in this role. Organizational culture is central to the success of UC San Diego Oncology, and the Senior Director must be an accessible, credible, and collaborative leader capable of building trust across diverse constituencies.

The incumbent must effectively lead within both direct and matrixed reporting structures and develop productive relationships with executive leaders, physicians, nursing leaders, APPs, faculty, staff, peers, and external partners.

The Senior Director will proactively partner with physician and administrative leaders to ensure effective, coordinated care throughout Oncology and Radiation Therapy Services. The physician-administrative-nursing dyad/triad partnership model is foundational to collaborative leadership and organizational success.

The Senior Director is expected to foster a culture of psychological safety, accountability, transparency, inclusion, professional respect, shared decision-making, and continuous improvement. The incumbent will model UC San Diego Health's values and create an environment in which leaders and staff are supported, challenged, developed, and empowered to perform at their highest level.
Oncology Representative and Spokesperson
The Senior Director serves as a principal representative and advocate for Oncology Nursing throughout UC San Diego Health.

The incumbent represents Oncology on the UC San Diego Health Nursing Executive Committee and collaborates closely with the Senior Director of Ambulatory Nursing, Chief Clinical Officer/Chief Nursing Officer, physician and administrative executives, and other senior leaders and cross-functional committees.

The Senior Director also maintains an appropriate external presence within professional associations, community organizations, academic and clinical networks, and oncology-focused organizations. The incumbent represents UC San Diego Health and Oncology Nursing in advancing professional practice, workforce development, patient advocacy, clinical excellence, and the evolving needs of patients and families affected by cancer.
Organizational Scope and Accountability

The Senior Director oversees, through subordinate leaders and managers, large and complex clinical departments and programs encompassing multiple functional disciplines and professional classifications. The position has significant organizational impact and responsibility for developing and administering policies, programs, systems, and strategic initiatives.

The incumbent manages significant human, financial, clinical, and physical resources and operates with a high degree of autonomy and executive accountability. The Senior Director ensures appropriate stewardship of departmental resources and oversees the development and implementation of systems, controls, policies, and procedures designed to protect organizational assets and support sustainable operational performance.

The Senior Director works collaboratively with executive leadership to develop short- and long-term strategies; leads complex organizational change; represents nursing on cross-functional and enterprise-wide committees; and ensures nursing care remains aligned with organizational policies, professional standards, accreditation requirements, regulatory requirements, and UC San Diego Health's strategic priorities.
Provides executive leadership, oversight, and accountability for the quality, safety, effectiveness, and consistency of nursing practice and patient care across UC San Diego Oncology.

Participates in appropriate professional associations, community organizations, and advocacy initiatives to advance oncology nursing, address the evolving health care needs of patients and families, and contribute to discussions involving workforce development, health care access, patient education, affordability, and cancer care delivery.
